# ticket-runner

> Write the ticket. It comes back done. Ponos, the ticket-runner robot, does the work on your machine while you do something else — a pull request, a text, an action — asks on Telegram or Slack when it needs you, and merges or publishes only once you say yes.

The loop is four gestures: you write a ticket and move it to *Ready*; Ponos does it, in a
Claude Code session (by default) on a disposable git worktree of its own; you read what came
back and answer in a word, even from your phone; you move it to *Validated* and he merges the
pull request or publishes the text, and only then calls it *Done*. The board is Notion by
default, or a folder of Markdown files; any model can be used through OpenRouter. Python
3.11+, standard library only — no dependency to install, no build step.

## Docs

- [Landing page](https://cardona.digital/ticket-runner/): the promise, the loop, the three proofs, the console, installation
- [Documentation](https://github.com/SalvadorCardona/ticket-runner#readme): installation, the board and its columns, the Validated column, recurring tickets, Telegram and Slack, the web console, the Markdown board, OpenRouter, several GitHub accounts, usage limits, configuration, safety, troubleshooting, Ponos the mascot
- [Changelog](https://github.com/SalvadorCardona/ticket-runner/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed, release by release
